fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**
Nothing. There is no material. At the size shown, everything that is not ground is a single flat colour, `#07080D`. You could not put a hand on it because there is no surface there to touch.

The one qualified exception: a band at **y 199–230, x 22–343 and x 405–730** does carry block courses — but its mean is `[4.2, 4.1, 5.0]` out of 255. At 1:1 it is invisible. I only found it after a 0.30 gamma lift.
fields.Q1_WHY:
I sampled the fill at five widely separated points and got the same value each time: `(20,500)→[6,7,11]`, `(340,100)→[7,8,13]`, `(470,60)→[7,8,13]`, `(400,800)→[7,8,14]`, `(740,490)→[6,6,8]`. Standard deviation across the whole south band (y 776–836, x 100–640) is `[0.66, 0.68, 1.01]`. That is not a dim material. That is a fill colour.

---
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR A FLAT PATTERN AROUND THE EDGE?**
**Flat pattern — a change of colour.** Not even a pattern; a change of colour.

What decided it: the boundary does not respond to the light. The figure is at x≈405. The band directly below them (x 400, y 800) is `[7,8,14]`. The band 300px away at the dark left corner (x 100, y 800) is `[7,8,13]`. Identical. Every lit thing in this image falls off with distance — the ground drops from 157 to 7 across the same span at y 490 — and this does not. It sits outside the lighting model entirely, which is what a background fill does and what a wall does not.

The *only* evidence of thickness anywhere is dimensional, not visual: the south band runs y 774–837, exactly 64px, and the north corridor is exactly 64px wide (x 375–438). So the grid cell is 64px and the wall is one cell thick. You can derive that. You cannot see it.

---
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**
Three edges, all the same treatment, all **2–3 pixels**:

- **South, x=220:** y 768 `[5,5,6]` → y 772 `[3,3,4]` (one dark seam) → y 776 `[7,8,13]` flat, held for 60px to the UI bar.
- **East, y=490:** x 716 = 7.6 lum → x 717–720 = 3.3 (seam) → x 721 = 5.8 flat to the frame.
- **West, y=490:** x 52 `[7,8,13]` → x 56 `[3,3,4]` (seam) → x 60 `[4,4,6]`.

What changes across it: brightness drops for two pixels, then goes flat. Nothing else. No bevel, no cast shadow onto the ground, no base course, no dirt or rubble in the join, no darkening ramp. The ground is cut off with a knife and a different colour is placed next to it.

Note the west edge inverts: the fill *outside* (`[7,8,13]`) is **brighter** than the ground *inside* it (`[4,4,6]`). The far corners of the room are darker than the void beyond them. That is backwards and it is why the room reads as floating rather than enclosed.

---
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**
**NOTHING.** There is no rope, no pin, no driven wedge, no timber, no hide strap, no bracket, no shoring anywhere on the standing structure. I checked the north band (y 199–230), both corridor flanks (x 342–372 and x 439–500, y 0–190), and all three room edges under magnification and lift. There is nothing to cut because nothing is doing any work.

Four hundred years of a company that repairs things endlessly, and their hands have touched nothing that stands up in this frame.

---
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR REPEATED?**
**Repeated.** One colour stamped across every cell that isn't ground. Where anything *is* drawn — the north band — it is two courses of the same block motif that is on the ground, at lower brightness. Nothing is stacked, nothing bears on anything, no course is offset to carry a load, no corner is resolved differently from a straight run. The north-east corner (x 700–730, y 230–260) and the south-west corner (x 55–90, y 740–775) are handled identically to the middle of a run: a seam and a fill.

---
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED?**
**YES.** It is legible, it runs at phone size, and the lighting falloff is real and smooth.

Merely competent or genuinely good? **Merely competent, and only because the ground is carrying it.** Judged on the standing structure alone — which is the brief — it is below competent, because there is no standing structure. The image works as a map. It does not work as a place.

---
fields.Q7:
AT 1:1, WHAT CAN YOU SEE ON THE STANDING SURFACES?**
**Blank.** At 1:1 there is no face of any material visible anywhere on the boundary. Not dim, not subtle — blank. The south band, the west band and the east band are a single uninflected tone from edge to edge.

- **Legible at 1:1:** the *silhouette* — where the room stops. Nothing else.
- **Only on magnification:** the block courses in the north band (y 199–230); a faint hairline in the north flat band (y 233–256); a few 2–3px blotches in the south band around x 150–260, y 790–820, at contrast under 3/255.

Does it change with distance from the figure? **No — and that is the finding.** The band immediately below the figure at (400, 800), which is as close as the boundary gets to the light, is exactly as blank as the band at (100, 800) in the far corner. The light reaches it and nothing happens. On the north side, the masonry band at x 380–440 — directly up-light from the figure — is at mean lum ~10, which is still black on a phone.
fields.Q7_WHY:
Checked at 1:1: `(100–640, 776–836)` south band; `(5–50, 300–700)` west band; `(722–749, 300–700)` east band; `(60–340, 233–256)` north flat band; `(342–372, 40–190)` corridor west flank. Had to magnify 4× **and** lift gamma to 0.30 before anything appeared in: `(22–343, 199–230)` and `(405–730, 199–230)` north masonry band; `(60–340, 233–256)` for the hairline.

---
fields.Q8:
ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**
Yes, two things.

1. **The colour `#07080D`.** It is at the top of the frame, the bottom of the frame, both sides of the room, both flanks of the north corridor, and in the gap between the north band and the room. Five sampled points, five identical values. Once you notice it you cannot stop noticing it: the entire non-ground half of this image is one hex value.

2. **The 2px seam.** Every boundary in the image terminates the same way — `[3,3,4]` for two pixels, then flat. South at y 772, east at x 717–720, west at x 56, and both corridor flanks. Same seam, same width, same value, every edge, every direction. Nothing is resolved differently anywhere.

Separately, and I'll flag it rather than judge it: there is a hard-edged flat light-grey rectangle at **x 183–247, y 455–518** sitting on top of the ground, with a matching fragment at **x 0–25, y 452–490**. Both at the same vertical band as the "RIG" bar. I read these as interface bleeding through rather than world geometry, so I'm leaving them out of scope — but if they are *not* interface, they are the most conspicuous unexplained objects in the frame.

---
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**
Two different nothings, and neither is a place.

- **The `#07080D` fill** — left of x 55, below y 774, right of x 721, and flanking the north corridor. Flat, unlit, textureless. This is out-of-bounds, not space. It is not "more of the same stuff" and it is not darkness either, because darkness would vary and this does not.
- **A separate near-black `[1,1,1]`** filling x 0–310, y 0–195 and x 500–750, y 0–195, with a scatter of isolated single pixels in it. Two distinct fills for two distinct states — presumably "unexplored" versus "known but unlit."

The **only** thing beyond the boundary that reads as a *place* is the masonry band at y 199–230. And because it uses the same block motif as the ground, what it says is "there is more ground up there" — not "there is a structure between you and it."

So: **something I cannot name, because it is not represented.** The image told me by having no gradient, no variance and no response to light in any of it.

---
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH FROM A DEAD END?**
Found it. The gap is at **x 375–438** — exactly one 64px cell — running north from the room edge at y 258 all the way to y 0.

I read it as **a passage**. But the difference was made entirely by out-of-scope material: the ground texture continues up the corridor unbroken, at a luminance that stays readable (column mean over x 380–430 is 56 at y 300, still 27 at y 250, versus the flanks at a dead-flat 6.4 with std 0.65). The ground going somewhere is what tells you it is a passage.

The structure contributes nothing to that read. The corridor's flanks are the same `#07080D` as the outside of the south wall, the outside of the west wall and the unreachable void. There is no jamb, no return, no thickening at the mouth, no corner where the room's edge turns to become the corridor's edge — the seam at y 258 simply stops at x 375 and resumes at x 438. If you deleted the ground layer you would not be able to find this opening at all.

That is the honest failure state: at 1:1 on a phone, a player reads passages off the floor. The walls are not participating in navigation.

---
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**
**No. Nothing has ever happened to it.** No damage, no settling, no repair, no patching, no soot, no water, no impact, no wear at contact points, no difference between one stretch of edge and another.

I read that from uniformity: south band std `[0.66, 0.68, 1.01]`, corridor flank std `[0.65, 0.63, 0.88]`. Those numbers are the signature of an untouched fill. Compare a ground sample at (300–400, 400–500): std `[35.1, 27.2, 17.5]`. All the history in this image is in the layer I'm not allowed to talk about. The layer I *am* looking at has no history at all — it is younger than everything around it, in a place that has been in continuous heavy use since before records.

---
fields.CULL: Rooms have no walls — the boundary is one flat unlit colour with a two-pixel cut.
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Give the boundary a top face with actual masonry at a value readable at 1:1 near the light — the north band's motif is the right idea at roughly 4× too dark, and it must exist on all four sides, not just north.
- Make the boundary respond to the light: the wall cell below the figure at (400, 774–837) must be visibly brighter than the same band at (100, 774–837). Right now they are the same three bytes.
- Resolve the ground/wall join with more than a 2px seam at y 772 / x 717 / x 56 — a base course, a cast shadow onto the ground, or debris in the corner, so the room reads as enclosed rather than cut out.
- Put the repair work on the standing structure: driven pins, lashed timber, salvaged plate over a breach — at least one visible at 1:1 per screen. Nothing currently holds anything up.
- Make the corridor mouth at x 375–438, y 258 readable from the structure alone: a jamb or thickened return at the opening, so the passage is legible with the ground layer hidden.

---

The whole picture rests on one layer. The ground is doing the material, the wear, the history, the lighting and the navigation; the structure is doing none of those and is, byte for byte, a single hex value. Fixing the wall value in isolation won't be enough — until the boundary responds to the torch, it will keep reading as a hole in the image rather than a thing standing in the room.
